issues.legal_issue: A special-leave order may be revoked when the petition contains material statements that are misleading and bear on the Court’s decision to grant leave.
material_facts: The appeal challenged the refusal to grant a certificate after the High Court had dismissed a writ petition concerning land-acquisition proceedings.
The certificate application to the High Court had been made only under the constitutional ground concerning a question of general importance.
The special-leave petition did not specify that limited ground and stated that the appellant was entitled to a certificate as of right under alternative value-based grounds.
The Court granted special leave without being told that the certificate application had been made only on the limited ground.
The Court had separately refused leave to appeal against the dismissal of the writ petition.
issues.conclusion: The Court revoked the order granting special leave and dismissed the appeal with costs.
issues.legal_principle: An applicant seeking special leave must correctly state all material facts bearing on the Court’s exercise of discretion and on maintainability. A statement calculated or likely to mislead on such a matter may justify revoking leave. The Court relied on Rajabhai Abdul Rehman Munshi v. Vasudev Dhanjibhai Mody and Hari Narain v. Badri Das (1964) 3 SCR 203, and applied this principle to the special-leave jurisdiction under Article 136; the certificate application had been made under Article 133(1)(c), whereas the petition asserted entitlement under Article 133(1)(a) or (b).

rule.if: special_leave_appeal and certificate_application_limited and petition_omits_application_limit and petition_claims_alternative_entitlement and statements_likely_to_mislead

predicates.special_leave_appeal: The applicant seeks appellate review after the Court has granted special leave.
predicates.certificate_application_limited: The applicant's earlier application for a certificate was made only on a limited ground.
predicates.petition_omits_application_limit: The special-leave petition does not disclose the limited ground on which the earlier certificate application was made.
predicates.petition_claims_alternative_entitlement: The special-leave petition asserts entitlement to a certificate on alternative grounds not stated in the earlier application.
predicates.statements_likely_to_mislead: The petition's statements are calculated or likely to mislead the Court on a matter bearing on its decision to grant leave.

issues.definition: When an applicant appeals after receiving special leave, omits that the earlier certificate application was limited, claims alternative entitlement, and thereby makes statements likely to mislead, the special leave is revoked.
